_README: Curated drug knowledge base for the deterministic medication-safety layer (backend/services/medication_safety.py). This is the OFFLINE source of truth for the demo: ingredient normalization, product->ingredient composition (to catch HIDDEN duplicate active ingredients, e.g. acetaminophen inside a cold combo), drug->class mapping (for allergy matching), allergy cross-reactivity, and a small pairwise interaction table. The medication_safety service can OPTIONALLY enrich this from RxNorm/RxNav (name normalization) and openFDA (label/interaction text) when network is available and results are cached — but the deterministic allergy / duplicate-ingredient / interaction checks never depend on a network call. openFDA interaction data is unstructured label prose, so a curated pairwise table is used as the reliable deterministic source. Pediatric portfolio/demo only; not validated for clinical use.

allergy_cross_reactivity.note: There is a small chance of cross-reaction between penicillins and cephalosporins. With a penicillin allergy, a cephalosporin should be given only on your pediatrician's advice.

aspirin.reason: Aspirin is linked to Reye's syndrome — a rare but life-threatening illness — when given to children or teenagers, especially during a viral illness. Do not give aspirin to a child for fever or pain unless a pediatric specialist has specifically prescribed it.

interactions.note: Ibuprofen and naproxen are both NSAIDs. Taking them together gives no extra benefit and raises the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems. Use only one NSAID at a time.
Ibuprofen and aspirin are both NSAIDs; combining them increases the risk of stomach bleeding. (Aspirin should not be used in children regardless.)
Naproxen and aspirin are both NSAIDs; combining them increases bleeding risk. (Aspirin should not be used in children regardless.)
Ibuprofen (an NSAID) markedly increases the bleeding risk in someone taking the blood thinner warfarin. Do not combine without explicit medical direction.
Naproxen (an NSAID) increases the bleeding risk in someone taking warfarin. Do not combine without explicit medical direction.
Aspirin increases bleeding risk in someone taking warfarin.
Regular acetaminophen use can raise the INR (blood-thinning effect) in someone taking warfarin. Occasional use is usually fine, but mention regular use to the prescriber.
Diphenhydramine and cetirizine are both antihistamines. Using them together adds to drowsiness and side effects without added benefit.
Diphenhydramine and loratadine are both antihistamines. Using them together adds side effects without added benefit.
Pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine are both decongestants. Combining them adds to heart-rate and blood-pressure effects without added benefit.
